answer_part:
The CONTROL device formulation employs m-MeO-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL as a surface passivator within the perovskite precursor solution, alongside MACl at 15.0 mg/mL. While m-MeO-PEACl provides some defect passivation at grain boundaries and interfaces, its meta-substituted methoxy group disrupts optimal molecular packing due to steric hindrance, leading to incomplete coverage of undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites and iodide vacancies. This results in elevated trap-assisted recombination, particularly at perovskite grain boundaries and the perovskite/SAM interface, which manifests as voltage losses and reduced charge extraction efficiency. Consequently, the CONTROL device exhibits a Voc of 1.17607 V, Jsc of 25.3513 mA/cm², FF of 79.1751%, and PCE of 23.606%, with the primary limitation being non-radiative recombination losses that suppress Voc and FF. The meta-orientation also impedes uniform monolayer formation, causing localized shunting paths that further degrade FF and long-term stability against ion migration.

Replacing m-MeO-PEACl with its para-isomer counterpart, p-MeO-PEACl, at an identical concentration of 2.0 mg/mL addresses these limitations through enhanced molecular alignment. The para-substituted methoxy group enables linear, face-on orientation on perovskite surfaces, strengthening binding to defect sites via optimal orbital overlap and hydrogen bonding with surface halides. This suppresses trap-assisted recombination more effectively, reducing interfacial energy losses and improving quasi-Fermi level splitting. The resulting denser, more homogeneous passivation layer minimizes shunting pathways, enhances hole extraction at the perovskite/SAM interface, and stabilizes the lattice against halide migration. These changes collectively elevate charge carrier lifetime and mobility, directly boosting Voc and FF while improving film morphology to increase Jsc. Although p-MeO-PEACl at this concentration slightly increases hydrophobicity, the trade-off is favorable as it mitigates moisture ingress without compromising charge transport, unlike higher concentrations that could introduce insulating barriers.

The optimized formulation maintains all other components unchanged: Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅I₃ precursor at 1.65 mol/L, MACl at 15.0 mg/mL, 4,4,4-NA SAM at 0.5 mg/mL in ethanol, and PDADI passivation at 0.5 mg/mL in IPA. Performance improvements are quantified as follows: Voc increases to a range of 1.17–1.20 V, Jsc rises to 26.42–26.60 mA/cm², FF improves to 79.3–81.3%, and PCE reaches 24.51–25.95%. These gains stem from reduced recombination losses and enhanced interfacial energetics, with the para-isomer’s superior passivation directly resolving the meta-isomer’s steric limitations in the CONTROL device.

Implement the following formulation adjustment:  
- Replace m-MeO-PEACl with p-MeO-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL in the perovskite precursor solution.
control_device_fabrication: The champion target devices showed a JSC of 25.3513 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.17607 V, and a FF of 79.1751%, resulting in a PCE of 23.606%. Perovskite precursor solution (1.65 mol/L) was prepared based on the stoichiometric ratio of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3. A SAM solution consisting of 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) in ethanol was prepared. To prepare the precursor solutions with MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and m-MeO-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL), the additives were added to the precursor solution. The perovskite precursor solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. At last 15 s, the injection of 150 µL antisolvent aided in reducing defect density within the perovskite layer. Then the substrate was annealed at 110 °C for 15 min to form the perovskite layer. Later, the 0.5 mg/mL PDADI (in IPA) was evenly spread on the surface of the perovskite film. The passivation layer was spin-coated at 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the spin-coating of the passivation layer, 70 µL of passivator was added at 6 s. To ensure optimal passivation, the layer was annealed at 100 °C for 5 min. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
target_device_fabrication: The combined treatment featured a PCE of 25.3859%, FF of 80.2987%, Voc of 1.18778 V, and Jsc of 26.6164 mA/cm². The Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3 precursor solution (1.65 mol/L) was prepared in the mixed solvent of DMF and DMSO. Different concentrations of 4,4,4-NA were added into the perovskite precursor solution for modification. For the additives treated cells, the MACl (15.0 mg/mL) or p-MeO-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) were added into the perovskite precursor solution. A meticulously timed spin procedure included 1000 rpm for 5 s, succeeded by 5500 rpm for 30 s to refine crystal growth. Antisolvent (150 µL) was dripped onto the center of film at 15 s before the end of spin-coating. A post-deposition anneal at 110 °C for 15 min stabilized the absorber layer and enhanced device performance. A passivation layer, PDADI (0.5 mg/mL), was incorporated into the system. Then the passivation solution was spin-coated onto the as-prepared perovskite films at a speed of 5000 rpm for 30 s. At a timing of 6 s, 70 µL of passivator was introduced into the spinning passivation layer. The passivation layer was then annealed at 100 °C for 5 min to enhance film quality. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
